nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 37.2.6-37.4.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 Pro, version 24H2, OS build 26100.4652 ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version n/a ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Expect the Windows Mica and Acrylic effect to work consistently. ### Actual Behavior Fix #47386 was supposed to address the issue, but it doesn't work on v37.2.6 (when the patch was first introduced) and higher v37.x.x releases. If the application window is dragged partially off screen, the screen that left the display will be black when dragging back. If the app window is completely covered then the entire app background color goes black. While the application body does not work, the titlebar does have the mica/acrylic affect. I've tried using the "backgroundMaterial" BrowserWindow options property and "setBackgroundMaterial()" method, but it has the same results. If using Electron v38-alpha8 or higher, it works as long as Windows 11's "Energy saver" option is turned off. If W11 Energy saver is turned on the app window background and titlebar turns a shade of gray. Testing was done using both my own app and Electron Fiddle with both having the same results. With Fiddle, the only code change from the default templates is adding backgroundMaterial property to the BrowserWindow options. Edited for clarity after further testing. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/85b8b48ddd9325b1b62bb8bf3ed705d1 ### Additional Information _No response_

nodes.title: Deprecate & remove `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT` env var
nodes.body:
### Timeline

* **Deprecation**: Electron 38
* **Removal**: Electron 39

### Background

While working on the [main upgrade roll](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/47983) for Electron 39, [this change](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6819616) that removes the `--ozone-platform-hint` flag was causing an error. After tracking it back to a change, I discovered the flag was being removed because [the default value became `auto`](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6775426). That change landed in [Chromium 140](https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/commit/3cf2a1826b002326a2d2994a489e98eebc340054) which is part of Electron 38.

Curious about our env var's intended behavior, I searched through the history of it. I learned it was [added](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/39792) to make it simple for users to tell Electron apps to automatically detect Wayland.[^1] Since the `auto` behavior is now the default, `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT`'s purpose is equivalent to `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` and we can remove it without losing any convenience for those Wayland users.

I also noticed the flag removal in Chromium is also being [backported to Chromium 140](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6824606). We should keep the environment variable "working" for Electron 38 to give users time to adapt if something unexpected comes up. If we decide that the risk is not large enough, we can also choose to do the removal in Electron 38, but I'm planning to do the removal in Electron 39.

The removal will be backwards-compatible, so users running apps with Electron 38 and below will continue to accept the `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT` and Electron 39 and above will safely ignore it.

[^1]: It can also be set to `wayland` to force Wayland instead of potentially falling back to X11; however, `auto` works by inspecting the `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` env var, meaning ours now acts like an alias for that one.

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

### Problem

How can the app callback signal to the `getDisplayMedia()` caller that it wants to abort the window selection and deny the screen share?

### Reproduction

1. Some page JS calls `await navigator.getDisplayMedia()`. For the page, the call stalls here.
2. On the web, this would call the browser UI to select a window to share. In Electron, this calls the app handler that was passed to `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()`.
3. The app handler then brings up a UI dialog to allow the user to select the window to share
4. The user aborts the selection, by clicking [Cancel], because he changed his mind and doesn't want to share the screen.
5. To signal the abort, the UI dialog throws an exception into the handler.
(There is no other way to tell electron `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` and the waiting `getDisplayMedia()` that the selection was aborted.)

### Expected result
1. `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` catches the exception
2. It throws the same exception into the caller of `getDisplayMedia()`.
3. This terminates the screen share in a defined way.
4. The UI that called `getDisplayMedia()` catches the exception and handles it.



### Actual Behavior

1. `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` doesn't catch the exception
2. This triggers an `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning`.
3. The screen sharing now hangs.
4. Starting another screen sharing will cause `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler()` or `desktopCapturer.getSources()` (?) to throw, causing another `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning`.
5. In some cases, the problem persists **even after an app restart**. I've observed that multiple times myself, on Linux. This suggests that something goes badly wrong.

nodes.title: [Feature] Expose NSMenuItem.alternate in Menu API
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The NSMenuItem class on macOS supports an "[alternate](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsmenuitem/isalternate?language=objc)" property, allowing a pair of adjacent sibling menu items to be joined together into what the user perceives as a single visible item that changes its title, key-equivalent, and behavior depending on what modifier keys are held.

For instance, in the File menu, Chrome's "Close All" item is an alternate of the preceding "Close Tab", available when holding the alt/option key. Safari similarly has "Close Other Tabs" as an alternate of "Close Tab".

This functionality is useful, but is not currently exposed by Electron.

### Proposed Solution

It should be fairly straightforward to add a `base::flat_map<int, bool> alternateFlags_;` to `ElectronMenuModel`, expose it to C++ and JS, and do something like this in `electron_menu_controller.mm `:
```objective-c++
    if (model->IsAlternateAt(index))
      [item setAlternate:YES];
```

Note that it would also be useful to support alternate pairs that *don't* have accelerators (but do have modifier masks). This is done by calling `setKeyEquivalentModifierMask` without `setKeyEquivalent` (or by calling `setKeyEquivalent` with an empty string). This is used in Chrome for eg "Tab -> Duplicate Selected Tab", which is an alternate of `Tab -> Duplicate Tab` with a modifier mask of `Option`. This could probably be implemented by skipping the `setKeyEquivalent` call if `character <= 0`, though I'm not sure if there are other API/parser issues there.

### Alternatives Considered

Apps can already update their menus (and behavior) manually in response to key events, but this is clunky for the developer, and doesn't offer the full functionality that the alternate flag does. With the alternate flag, the user is able to rebind the keyboard shortcut for either or both of the menu items in System Settings, with the UI automatically updating accordingly.

Apps can also simply add all actions to their menus without setting the alternate flag, but this can result in an excessively-cluttered menu.

### Additional Information

This was previously proposed in #20902, but it was closed out as "completed" by the filer despite not actually being implemented.

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS 15.6

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

27.3.11

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

`<video>` tag should work with any video, also HDR video.

To reproduce: https://github.com/mifi/electron-mas-video-bug

It should show a video player that allows playing back the video, this expected behaviour can be seen by simply running the unsigned app:
```
npx electron src/index.js
```


### Actual Behavior

Since Electron 27.3.11, the bug appears:

With the [example](https://github.com/mifi/electron-mas-video-bug), observe that the window goes completely blank (background color is still visible). It's sometimes flashing if you move your mouse around in the window. Not only the `<video>` goes blank but the whole rendering of the window content blanks out, even chrome dev tools stops working. Once the video is hidden or removed from the DOM, the rendering recovers and all content re-appears. It does not crash the app in any way, the app is still interactive, even the UI that is not being rendered is still interactive, and the video can be played back (with audio). Once the `<video>` element is removed, or the `src` is set to a different video, the rendering instantly recovers.

- Downgrading Electron to 27.3.11 works (no bug).
- Electron version from 28.0.0 until 28.1.1 app hard crashes on launch (even non-signed)
- Electron versions from 28.1.2 until 37.2.5 shows the bug


### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/mifi/electron-mas-video-bug

### Additional Information

This bug can also be seen with the Mac App Store version of my app [LosslessCut](https://github.com/mifi/lossless-cut)

nodes.title: The size of temporary file created by Electron always increase when loading images
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 37.2.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When Electron app launches, it creates a `{uuid}.tmp` file in the `C:\Users\{username}\AppData\Local\Temp ` folder. If the Electron app does not contain any images, the size of this file is always 0 byte. If the Electron app displays multiple images, the size of this file increases proportionally to the images size. The size of this `tmp` file can grow unbounded to 10GB for some of our users. Expected behavior: the file size should not grow unbounded and cause the hard disk to run out of space. ### Actual Behavior The size of the `tmp` file increases and can cause hard disk to run out of space. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/thomasdao/74f9d9996ce7dea50dd86c72bfc0f2bf ### Additional Information In File Explorer, it's easier to sort the files in Temp folder by "Date modified" descending, so the `uuid`.tmp file created by this sample appears on top. You need to press "Delete" key to try to delete the file, then the system will show a warning this file is being used by Electron, and show the most updated size of the file. Please note that due to system caching, you may need to wait for up to 30 seconds and try deleting a few times for the real size to be shown in the warning dialog.
